neighbours.label: The word-piece 'ij' / 'iy' / 'ih' inside a proper name, right after the name's opening consonant piece (N|ij|megen, N|iy|ogi, N|ih|alani, K|ij|ko, Mat|ij|evic); names beginning with a whole-token Ni- (Nigeria, Nicaragua) stay quiet
fire: The train from Arnhem stops at Nijmegen before it crosses the river.
The exhibition honours the dancer Vaslav Nijinsky and his sister.
The lecture was given by Professor Niyogi from the climate institute.
Critics praised the early films of Govind Nihalani for their realism.
The rover team dedicated the mission to engineer Jake Matijevic.
The earthquake catalogue was compiled by Andrzej Kijko and his students.
The poet Martinus Nijhoff translated several English plays into Dutch.
The president at the time was Saparmurat Niyazov of Turkmenistan.
quiet: The train from Arnhem stops at Utrecht before it crosses the river.
The exhibition honours the dancer Rudolf Nureyev and his teacher.
The lecture was given by Professor Nielsen from the climate institute.
Critics praised the early films of Satyajit Ray for their realism.
The rover team dedicated the mission to engineer Jake Morrison.
The earthquake catalogue was compiled by Charles Richter and his students.
The poet from Nigeria translated several English plays into Yoruba.
The president at the time was Richard Nixon of the United States.

notes: Card: peak tokens 'ij' x11, 'iy' x7, 'ih' x1 inside Dutch, South Asian and Slavic names. Probes: Niyogi 1.03, Nijmegen 0.76, Nijinsky 0.61, Kijko 0.57, Matijevic 0.57, Nihalani 0.56; Utrecht 0.00, Nigeria/Nicaragua 0.01. A spelling-unit label: it depends on the tokenizer splitting the name after the first consonant piece, which I could only check through probing.
